title: Laredo College Veterans Day observance puts a student veteran's voice at the center
excerpt: Laredo College held its annual Veterans Day Observance on Wednesday at the Pvt. David B. Barkley Cantu Veterans Memorial Chapel, with U.S. Army veteran and LC student Dinorah Villarreal delivering the keynote address.
content:
Laredo College held its annual Veterans Day Observance on Wednesday at the Pvt. David B. Barkley Cantu Veterans Memorial Chapel on the Ft. McIntosh campus, with a U.S. Army veteran who is now an LC student delivering the keynote address, according to the college.

The chapel is named for the Laredo native, World War I hero and first Hispanic recipient of the Medal of Honor. The Ft. McIntosh campus itself carries military history dating back to 1849. Local veterans representing various military conflicts and branches filled the chapel pews as the Laredo College Police Department Honor Guard presented the United States and Texas flags.

This year's keynote speaker was Dinorah Villarreal, a U.S. Army veteran, LC student veteran, educator, mother and community leader. The college said her journey reflects the resilience, determination and commitment to lifelong learning shown by many veterans moving from military service to civilian life.

“I found myself beginning another mission. This time my mission was in a classroom,” Villarreal said.

She told veterans who believe too much time has passed to return to school that they are not starting from zero — they bring years of experience, discipline, leadership and problem-solving into the classroom, according to the college.

Albert Hernandez, the college's Director of Veterans Services, said Villarreal's story reinforces the message that a veteran's service to the nation may conclude, but the journey of growth, leadership and service to others continues. He called Veterans Day an opportunity to honor the courage, sacrifices and dedication of the men and women who served in the U.S. Armed Forces, and said the observance holds special significance at Laredo College as it recognizes not only their military service but also their continued contributions to the college and community.

Laredo College President Dr. Minita Ramírez recalled having family members in the military and how their service shaped her view of honoring those who served. She said military service touches the entire family and becomes part of its history and memories, and that the greatest tribute to those who served is to live in a manner worthy of what they gave.

Sources: Laredo College, “LC Veterans Day Observance spotlights student veteran’s voice” (Nov. 11, 2026).
